neighbours.label: ' bacteria' / ' bacterial' when set against viruses in the same sentence (viral rather than bacterial; viruses, bacteria and fungi)
fire: Most sore throats are viral, so a doctor will prescribe antibiotics only when the cause is bacterial.
The vaccine protects against the virus but offers no defence against bacteria that enter the wound.
Pneumonia may follow the flu when a virus weakens the lungs and bacteria move in.
Hand sanitiser kills many viruses, though some bacteria survive it in spore form.
The clinic can tell within an hour whether the fever comes from a virus or from bacteria.
Researchers screened the river water for viruses, bacteria and parasites after the storm.
A viral cold can turn into a bacterial sinus infection after a week or so.
Viruses need a host cell to multiply, whereas bacteria divide freely in warm food.
quiet: Most sore throats are viral, so a doctor will prescribe rest and fluids rather than medicine.
The vaccine protects against the virus but offers no defence against parasites that enter the wound.
Pneumonia may follow the flu when a virus weakens the lungs and fluid builds up.
Hand sanitiser dries the skin, though some brands add oils to soften it.
The clinic can tell within an hour whether the fever comes from a virus or from heat stroke.
Researchers screened the river water for pesticides, metals and plastics after the storm.
Yeast and helpful bacteria turn the milk into a thick sour yogurt overnight.
Fungi need a damp surface to spread, whereas mould spores drift freely in dry air.

notes: Card: ' bacterial' x4, ' bacteria' x4, ' bacter' x2, mostly next to 'viral'/'viruses'; also ' Frame', ' photos', ' color', which the label does not cover. Probes: with a virus mention 0.32-0.43; bacteria alone 0.02-0.19; 'compression format, color depth' 0.41. The + pole fires on virus-biology terms (replication, genus, -virus), so the two poles may split virus from bacterium.
